## 12. Losers with two matching pairs (one high tier)  -  PASS - No exceptions were noted

*Procedure:* Check whether at least 75% of losing tickets have two or more matching pairs, at least one pair being a high-tier symbol.

- 1,545,909 of 1,960,117 losers (78.87%) have >=2 matching pairs with at least one high-tier pair.
- No exceptions were noted. The proportion meets the 75% minimum (01/2025 series returned 79%).

## 13. Losers with one matching pair (high/mid tier)  -  PASS - No exceptions were noted

*Procedure:* Check whether at least 20% of losing tickets have exactly one matching pair with a high- or mid-tier symbol.

- 414,208 of 1,960,117 losers (21.13%) have exactly one matching pair with a high- or mid-tier symbol.
- Specification note: Game Spec section 5.1 states 70% here, which cannot hold alongside the 75% two-pair rule (they would sum to 145%). The Data Generation Spec states 20%; the 01/2025 series returned 21%. This procedure applies the 20% figure - Game Spec 5.1 should be corrected before sign-off.
- No exceptions were noted. The proportion meets the 20% minimum.

## 15. Print imposition order  -  PASS - No exceptions were noted

*Procedure:* Supplementary to the 14 procedures above (not part of the EY set). The file is in print-imposition order (7 channels, 56 cards per page) and is padded with VOID cards to keep pages aligned, so a rigid position formula does not apply. This procedure verifies the two properties that must hold regardless of padding: within each page the real cards step through the seven channels in non-decreasing order, and each channel's real cards ascend in (book, ticket). Procedures 9-11 and 14 de-interleave to serial order and are unaffected by this ordering.

- 5,800 VOID padding card(s) were seen and skipped for the order check (leading page fill plus band-boundary fill). The documented 7 x 5 channel table does not tile 30,000 books evenly, which is why padding is required; confirm the padding scheme with the data generation team.
- A PageNo / leading identifier column precedes the serial (not part of the documented record layout); 50+ distinct value(s) observed, e.g. 000001, 000002, 000003, 000004, 000005 .... Used here to delimit pages.
- No ordering exceptions were noted: real cards step through the channels in order within every page and each channel ascends in serial.
